item.title: Chocolate MC Sued Over Alleged Assault Of Teen After Las Vegas Club Show
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Chocolate MC faces a Vegas civil suit over an alleged assault after a club show, with the nightclub and hotel owner also named.
item.content:encoded:
Chocolate MC is being sued over the alleged sexual assault of a teen after a Las Vegas club show. The club and hotel owner Boyd Gaming also faces claims.

The Las Vegas Review-Journal reported the plaintiff was 16 at the alleged assault. Her lawyers sued Chocolate MC, whose legal name is Yosvanis Sierra Hernandez, on October 13.

The complaint says Masque Nightclub let her obtain alcohol and cocaine on December 31, 2024. It alleges Chocolate MC gave her more drugs and alcohol before sexually assaulting her at The Orleans.

The suit faults Masque’s owners for underage drinking and Boyd for failing to protect her. It seeks more than $15,000 on each of 13 claims.

The Review-Journal found no related criminal charge. Boyd declined to comment, and the club’s registered agent did not reply. The report did not include a response from Chocolate MC.

The Nevada suit is separate from the Florida case that put Chocolate MC in prison, which grew from the 2024 killing of Cuban reggaeton star El Taiger.

Prosecutors accused Damian Valdez-Galloso of killing the singer and Chocolate MC of trying to have Valdez-Galloso killed in jail.

A Miami jury found Chocolate MC guilty of soliciting first-degree murder in November 2025, the Miami Herald reported from his one-day trial.

Prosecutors said he used social media and an interview to offer inmates $20,000 in commissary money, then raised the sum to $100,000. They argued the posts could solicit violence without a direct message to an inmate and cited a song used in one post as evidence of intent.

Chocolate MC took the stand to deny trying to get anyone killed and said his posts were meant to promote an album.

He told jurors he had known El Taiger for about 20 years. His lawyer described the statements as a joke made in grief, but the jury rejected that position.

His conviction left other Florida charges unsettled, including accusations of threatening and abducting a fan.

In March, Chocolate MC accepted a plea agreement covering the solicitation count and separate cases, Univision Miami reported from the hearing. The deal brought a 10-year prison sentence followed by five years of probation.

item.title: Summer Walker’s Label Battle Reaches Point Of No Return Amid Fraud Accusations
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Summer Walker accused LVRN of withholding merch and YouTube income as she sought damages and an end to her 2017 agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Summer Walker sued Love Renaissance for fraud and sought to end her label and management deal over money she claimed the company kept.

The case became public this week through reporting by Rolling Stone and Billboard. Summer Walker filed the suit August 28, weeks before Interscope brought its separate $50 million claim against her.

Summer Walker accused LVRN of taking funds set aside for her tours, music, marketing and merchandise. She claimed the firm used those budgets to cover excessive company costs.

The disputed income included Amazon sales of goods carrying her name and image. Summer Walker alleged that LVRN sold those items through Amazon and other sites but failed to pay her a share of the sales.

She also accused LVRN of running a YouTube account she hadn’t known about. She claimed the firm erased the account’s past data before putting her in charge and never paid her any income from it.

Her lawyer, Keith Moten, said on Tuesday that her main goal was to end the deal.

“Most importantly, we also have very strong legal grounds for the court to order Summer’s release from her deal with LVRN as well,” Moten told Rolling Stone.

Billboard reported that Summer Walker described a deal that gave LVRN control beyond her music. She said it covered touring, merchandise and use of her name and image. Summer Walker alleged that no independent lawyer advised her before she signed.

Her fight with LVRN began before Interscope sued her on October 9. She had told Interscope she would stop working under its deal as of August 27, citing California’s seven-year rule. Interscope sought damages over recordings it said she still owed under a five-album commitment, while Summer Walker disputed its claims.

LVRN had moved toward a wider independent business, but it kept ties to Interscope involving Summer Walker.

In a June interview, LVRN CEO Tunde Balogun said the companies still worked together on Summer Walker and 6lack. For its broader business, LVRN chose Sony-owned The Orchard to distribute its music.

The new allegations followed a different public account of her deal in 2021. Summer Walker pushed back on reports about her original contract at the time, saying her terms had changed and she had her own representation and LVRN’s support.

LVRN did not respond to either outlet’s request for comment before their Tuesday reports. Summer Walker sought damages as well as an order voiding her September 15, 2017, agreement with the company.

item.title: Chance The Rapper Wins Against Ex-Manager Again After $35 Victory
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chance the Rapper won a new ruling against Pat Corcoran over merchandise profits after his earlier $35 jury victory.
item.content:encoded:
Chance the Rapper won another round against Pat Corcoran after a judge ordered his former manager to hand over undisclosed merchandise profits, months after the rapper won a courtroom battle that netted him just $35.

Cook County Circuit Court Judge James E. Hanlon Jr. ruled on October 13 that Corcoran breached his duties to Chance by seeking side payments from merchandise vendors without telling him. Rolling Stone, which obtained the ruling, reported that the repayment order covered vendor commissions and merchandise-related management fees.

The court ordered Corcoran to return those profits, along with the 15% management commissions he earned on merchandise during the period at issue. The court also directed him to hand over chanceraps.com, the domain used to sell the artist’s merchandise.

The amount still needs to be worked out. Chance’s representatives said they could recover as much as $1.5 million in management fees, plus vendor payments. The judge had not set a final dollar figure. A court conference in late November is set to address the calculation, Billboard reported.

“I’m grateful to finally close this chapter of my life and can’t wait to eventually tell my side of the story. I’m thankful to the courts and, more importantly, to God for remaining faithful,” Chance said in a statement supplied by his representatives.

The new decision covered a claim the judge heard in May, separate from the jury trial that ended in March.

That jury rejected Corcoran’s $3.8 million demand for unpaid commissions and awarded Chance $35 on his own counterclaims. The dispute over the manager’s duty to act in his client’s interests still had to be decided.

Corcoran sued in 2020 after Chance fired him that April. Their working relationship had begun in 2012, but they never signed a written management contract.

The former manager argued that their verbal deal entitled him to a share of income for three years after the split. Chance denied agreeing to those continued payments.

Their fight also reached beyond post-split income. Corcoran’s side argued that he should earn commissions on deals he worked on while employed, even though the money arrived later.

Chance’s lawyers accused him of pursuing his own profit through merchandise arrangements rather than protecting the artist’s business.

The judge rejected Chance’s request that Corcoran forfeit all past compensation, preserving payment for work outside the disputed merchandise arrangements.

Corcoran’s spokesperson emphasized that limit in a response to Rolling Stone and argued that Chance still had to prove harm in the merchandise business.

“The court ruled there is no basis for Chance’s claim of more than $10 million in damages,” the spokesperson said.

item.title: Drakeo The Ruler’s Estate Reaches Settlement In Live Nation Battle
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Drakeo The Ruler's family spent years fighting promoters over backstage security after his fatal 2021 festival stabbing.
item.content:encoded:
Drakeo The Ruler‘s estate reached a conditional settlement with Live Nation, TMZ reported. Financial details weren’t specified.

The family’s fight over backstage safety had stretched for years after the Los Angeles rapper was fatally stabbed at the Once Upon A Time in LA festival. He was 28 when he was attacked behind the main stage on December 18, 2021, and later died at a hospital.

On December 20, 2021, his mother, Darrylene Corniel, told Rolling Stone that venue security had failed her son.

“This happened backstage at an event. Someone has to be held accountable,” Corniel said.

She told the outlet that witnesses had described a large crowd overwhelming the small group that accompanied her sons. His brother, Ralfy The Plug, had tried to protect him, she said.

Corniel also described being unable to hug or kiss her son at the hospital. She had to see him through a window because his death was being treated as a homicide.

“I will not rest until justice is served,” she said in that interview.

Separate complaints followed from his mother, brother and son. In January 2023, Rolling Stone reported that Judge Yolanda Orozco allowed his brother and members of their Stinc Team collective to pursue claims against Live Nation and other defendants.

They alleged that vehicle searches were inadequate, guards were absent from the backstage VIP area, and nobody stopped the attack. Their claims included negligence, unsafe premises and emotional distress.

Live Nation argued that the attack was unforeseeable because no similar incident had occurred at the venue. Orozco ruled that the absence of a prior attack did not automatically bar their claims.

Judge James I. Montgomery had denied the estate’s request for financial records from Live Nation Worldwide and C3 Presents. Its lawyers argued that they had shown a strong likelihood of winning punitive damages, but Montgomery was not persuaded.

The promoters’ lawyers denied intentional wrongdoing. They said they hired a specialist to assess risks, plan security and coordinate vendors and law enforcement.

item.title: Tyler, The Creator Takes Over FC Barcelona Campaign & Calls His Own Shots
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Tyler, The Creator scored a Barcelona shirt takeover with creative control, limited GOLF jerseys and plans for a music event.
item.content:encoded:
Tyler, The Creator scored FC Barcelona’s Clásico shirts for GOLF WANG and took creative control of the takeover campaign.

Barcelona unveiled the deal on October 15, confirming that his brand’s GOLF logo will appear across the chest when the team faces Real Madrid on October 25.

The women’s team will wear the same design first, against Granada on October 24.

The deal gave Tyler and his brand full control of the campaign’s graphics and video, a first for an artist in the Spotify and Barcelona partnership.

A Tyler-directed short was part of the rollout.

His GOLF logo will replace the usual Spotify branding. That made him the ninth artist to take over the shirt under the sponsorship deal.

The design brought a new soccer stage to GOLF WANG, the fashion brand he founded in 2011.

“Tyler brings a distinct creative world to the collaboration, extending far beyond the jersey,” Marc Hazan, Spotify’s senior vice president of marketing and partnerships, said.

The fashion drop featured 11 pieces, with jackets, retro jerseys and other sportswear carrying the club and GOLF WANG names. It also included a scarf, socks and a bottle.

The launch came with plans for (The) Creator’s Àgora, a cultural space in Barcelona’s Gothic Quarter, scheduled for October 15 through October 25.

Barcelona artist Daniel2000 was tapped to direct the program. The program planned art, photography, performances, and DJ sets alongside the collection.

Fans could also see and shop the clothes there.

The match shirts came in several limited runs. The announced editions included 1,899 match-quality jerseys, another 22 signed by players from the men’s and women’s squads, and 11 signed by Tyler.

Tyler already had a fashion track record outside his own labels.

He unveiled a Louis Vuitton men’s capsule in February 2024 and thanked Pharrell Williams for helping him land the design opportunity.

He also followed two other major rap names onto Barcelona’s shirts. Drake and Travis Scott took part in earlier editions of the artist series.

The next stop is Copa De Golf on October 24. Yung Taco will headline the Barcelona event with a DJ set, joined by Bexnil, Alu, duna and Mushkaa, before the men’s Clásico the following day.

item.title: Nas Teases New Music With Powerful “BLAK MUSIC 2026” Statement
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Nas confirms he's working on music while delivering a powerful warning about exploitation, cultural amnesia and more!
item.content:encoded:
Nas has apparently been cooking up something bigger than another album, and his latest message suggests that Hip-Hop may be headed for a serious cultural reckoning.

The Queensbridge legend dropped a powerful statement on social media that reads like a manifesto, lesson and maybe new music.

And yes, he confirmed that he’s been working on music.

Nas opened by explaining that he has spent the past year observing the culture while creating new material. But rather than discussing producers, features or release dates, he took listeners on a historical journey from the Mississippi Delta to New Orleans and eventually New York.

He even invoked blues pioneer Robert Johnson, whose legendary crossroads mythology remains one of American music’s most fascinating stories.

Why would Nas bring up a blues musician from nearly a century ago?

Because he believes the music industry has a disturbing habit of forgetting the people who built it.

“The music game forgets or doesn’t compensate the foundation. Our greats have been stolen from and ripped off of.”

That’s a serious accusation and the the business – filthy as it is – is always under indictment.

Nas also questioned people’s obsession with temporary trends and the lack of unity among artists, executives and creators. He’s getting down to it.

“We gotta take a stand as one. It’s time for a celebration of the music.”

Now, here’s what has my attention – I know he’s not going to do the unthinkable…..

“BLAK MUSIC 2026”

Is that an album title? A new initiative? A cultural campaign? Perhaps something involving Mass Appeal?

Nobody has officially explained the designation yet. I am hoping for new music.

Interestingly, Nas has already spent considerable energy celebrating the architects through Mass Appeal’s Legend Has It… series, which brought new projects from several influential artists.

Could “BLAK MUSIC” represent an expansion of that movement?

Fans are already debating the message and what is means. I’m intrigued by the possibility that Nas wants to organize the culture around ownership, historical recognition and economic justice.

The man has certainly earned the right to initiate that conversation.

But let’s not mistake a compelling teaser for a confirmed album announcement. Nas has acknowledged making music, but he hasn’t identified a new release date or explained what “BLAK MUSIC 2026” means.

One thing is certain: Nas wants people to remember. Give the people something to remember!

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Cordae Hit With $15M Contract Lawsuit That May Derail Anderson .Paak Collab Album
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: MMMG sought millions and an order to stop new releases as it claimed Cordae’s 2018 recording deal remained in force.
item.content:encoded:
Cordae faced a new lawsuit eight days before his joint album with Anderson .Paak was due.

MMMG sued the rapper and three labels on October 15, claiming an old deal gave it control of his new music.

The 20-page complaint obtained by AllHipHop named EMPIRE, Apeshit and Mass Appeal alongside Cordae. It asked a New York federal court to halt releases that MMMG claimed violated its rights.

“Defendants never requested nor received a license from MMMG to release this album,” MMMG’s lawyer, Jeffrey M. Movit of Cohen & Gresser, wrote.

The label based its claims on a deal dated April 2018. It alleged that the deal still bound Cordae to record for MMMG alone.

The suit targeted “A Good Day,” the single and video released on September 16.

It also challenged the rollout of Heavy Is The Crown, set for October 23 through APESHIT + EMPIRE / Hi Level + Mass Appeal.

The fight reached beyond one song. MMMG alleged that Cordae had also kept its share of income from merch, touring and other work.

The company alleged that “he refuses to pay MMMG its contractual share of the revenues.”

The label traced the dispute to a change in how his music reached stores and streaming services.

It said Atlantic ended its deal on September 2, 2025. MMMG claimed it secured a new deal with Stem and told Cordae’s lawyers two days later.

That mattered because the contract allowed a six-month search for a new distributor, according to the suit.

MMMG alleged that its Stem deal kept Cordae’s contract alive. It said his lawyers later disputed whether that deal met the contract’s terms.

The complaint gave MMMG’s account of that exchange. No defense response appeared in the five public docket entries reviewed.

Cordae and Anderson .Paak’s ties stretched back to “RNP” in 2019.

Their song appeared on The Lost Boy, Cordae’s debut through ART@WAR and Atlantic. The new project took that partnership from guest spots to a shared album.

Cordae launched Hi Level in June 2021 while he was still signed to Atlantic. He made ownership a key part of his pitch for the new label.

For “A Good Day,” the suit sought at least $5 million or, as an alternative, damages set by copyright law.

It requested at least $15 million from Cordae for breach of contract. It also sought at least $5 million from the labels for allegedly causing that breach.

MMMG also asked for a jury trial and an order to bar further use of recordings it claimed it owned.

item.title: Cardi B’s Birkin Collection Takes A Hit As Esmeralda Goes Missing
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B said her Birkin Esmeralda is missing and thinks she left it in a hotel, calling it the only bag she can't find.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B said she lost the Hermès Birkin she named Esmeralda and thinks she left the purse behind at a hotel.

The rapper shared the news after a fan asked her to bring the bag back out. The request included an older clip of the brown leather purse.

“I fuvkin lost her ….its the only bag missing …I think I left her in a hotel and I’m so sad about it,” she wrote.

She had recently shown off a haul of new purses, including three Birkins she had bought over the span of a few weeks. Esmeralda isn’t the first purse to give her a headache.

In March 2025, she showed fans a mustard-yellow crocodile Birkin that her daughter had marked up. Cardi said that bag had cost her $60,000. She had first shown it off in October 2024 alongside two other new crocodile-skin bags.

Her hunt for rare pieces has taken her overseas before.

During a Vogue shoot at Paris Couture Week in July 2023, Cardi joked that she had really come to buy a Birkin. She said she spent two months looking for one she couldn’t find in the United States.

That collector’s eye became part of a business deal this year. On May 20, Fashionphile named Cardi its 2026 brand ambassador for the “Get Your Bag” campaign, which centered on shopping and reselling pre-owned luxury accessories.

She also curated a selection of her favorites for the platform, with pieces from Hermès, Chanel and Goyard.

Her picks included a crocodile Birkin 25 and a burgundy Chanel tote. The partnership brought her interest in rare finds and classics into the retailer’s shop-and-sell model.

Founder and president Sarah Davis said at the launch that Cardi understood the pieces’ value and could help broaden the audience for luxury resale.

Cardi pointed to its range of rare bags and classic styles, along with authenticity, as reasons the partnership made sense for her as a collector.

In her launch statement, Cardi summed up her taste: “I love a good bag, but I love a smart buy too.”

item.title: Police Find No Lil Baby Link To Keion White Shooting Suspects
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Police found no link between Lil Baby and Keion White's shooting suspects as one man was ordered released and another stayed jailed.
item.content:encoded:
Police have found no connection between Lil Baby and the suspects in Keion White’s shooting case, even as the nightclub attack moved into court.

KQED reported that finding after Gregory Walker and Curtis Green appeared at San Francisco’s Hall of Justice on Wednesday, October 14. A judge ordered Green released on misdemeanor gun charges, while Walker remained jailed without bail on felony counts.

The two men postponed entering pleas and were due back for arraignment Monday, October 19. The judge ordered both not to possess weapons.

Walker’s attorney, Jeff Wozniak, disputed the case against his client and said he would seek his release.

“We’re gonna show that he’s innocent, get him back to his family,” Wozniak said.

The court decisions added a new step after officials announced four arrests in the investigation. Police described a broader operation involving more than 50 search warrants and help from more than 250 law enforcement personnel.

White was hosting a private Super Bowl party downstairs at Dahlia’s in San Francisco when he was shot in the ankle early February 9.

The San Francisco Standard reviewed a police report in which a witness said Lil Baby’s entourage tried to enter White’s event.

The witness described an argument between White and the rapper, then heard gunfire while upstairs asking club managers for help. He told police he did not know who shot White.

Prosecutors alleged Walker and a second man awaiting charges fired guns, wounding the 49ers defensive lineman.

The district attorney’s office charged Walker with assault with a semiautomatic firearm and three felony gun-possession counts. It also alleged he personally fired a gun and caused great bodily injury.

Green’s charges were different. Prosecutors accused him of brandishing a firearm, carrying a concealed firearm and carrying a loaded firearm in public, all misdemeanors.

Authorities arrested Green in Irvine on October 7 and Walker in Los Angeles on October 9. Both were booked into San Francisco County Jail on October 12.

Police also identified Marquis Davis and Antoine Washington as suspects. Officials were still arranging their transfer to San Francisco when the court report was published.

The investigation remained open, with Walker and Green’s next court appearance set for Monday.

item.title: Kevin Hart Lands Fox Deal To Turn Short Dramas Into Films & TV
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kevin Hart's Hartbeat secured a Fox partnership built around 25 short dramas, adding a new route to film and television.
item.content:encoded:
Kevin Hart struck a new deal with Fox Entertainment that could turn phone-screen dramas from his Hartbeat company into films and full-length TV shows.

The lineup starts with 25 live-action shows, with thrillers, dramas and faith-based plots. They’ll debut on a Codeblack channel in My Drama, the video app run by Holywater Tech, under the Codeblack, Essence and Revolt brands.

Fox’s studio got the first chance to develop them into films and longer TV shows. Its global arm will sell the shorts abroad once their first runs on the app end.

The goal is to see what draws fans before making longer shows. The three brands have more than 20 million combined social followers, the companies said.

“Hartbeat has a powerful creative voice and an exceptional instinct for stories that connect with audiences,” Fox scripted chief Hannah Pillemer said in the deal announcement.

The move followed Hart’s defense of cuts at Hartbeat in May. Speaking on “The Breakfast Club,” he said his business had grown too large and needed to cut costs.

“My company was too big. I don’t need 80 people to operate how we’re operating now,” he said. “Downsize. Save the money.”

Hart said the cuts were meant to keep the business running well while he kept making films and shows through his own team. He pushed back at the idea that a smaller staff meant the end of Hartbeat.

In January, Hart took a stake in Authentic Brands Group as part of a deal to jointly own and run the Kevin Hart brand. The partners laid out plans to put his name on more products, digital ventures and live events.

His ties to Fox also predate this latest pact. Fox-owned Tubi announced a four-film Hartbeat deal in October 2025, built around stars who had already drawn fans online.

That deal included “Sundown,” written and directed by Kinigra Deon, who also starred, and “85 South: Dead End,” featuring DC Young Fly, Chico Bean and Karlous Miller. The two firms had worked together before, bringing Hartbeat films and shows to the free streaming service.

Hartbeat also struck a deal with aTwist in September for more than 20 original short shows. That slate included LOL comedies and plans to turn Blake Karrington’s books into series with Upscale Productions. Hartbeat could draw on fans of those books as it sought an audience for its new shows.

The Fox deal’s value was not disclosed. No films or full-length TV shows were named.
